Held at Brighton in perfect weather only John Knifton and Ken Bailey showed good form, with the team having to be content with 6th place. Surrey W.C. took the title, thanks to Fullager and Nihill who were 1st and 2nd!
Fotheringham (94.48) finished 9th, 22nd and 29th respectively, and the Kent championship at Bexley where Ken Bailey walked well to finish 9th in 87.26.
The 'A' team finished 10th, with Ray Middleton 6th (97.04), Ken Bailey 32nd (109-13), Cyril Yescombe 33rd (109-27), and George Bates 44th (111.24); 111 finished.

Ken Bailey and George Beecham were also showing good form in the twenties. Ken Bailey was unable to finish owing to stomach trouble, and from a possible second place the team were obliged to finish third with 71 points behind Leicester's 25 and Sheffield's 45.
BOTTOM LEFT: Belgrave's winning London Brighton Walk team seen passing through Clapham. K.

Don Thompson soon disappeared into the distance leaving Nigel Thompson of the Met. disputing 2nd place with our own Ken Bailey. Unfortunately Ken was to pay the price for an early fast pace, but he did carry off the handicap by some six minutes.
In the early stages George Beecham, Ken Bailey and Ray Hall walked together, but the pack broke up at ten miles with Ken chasing after the leaders.
In the circumstances Ray Hall John Knifton, Bob Barnes and Ken Bailey put up sterling performances and we were not disgraced by our final fifth position.
Also in close attendance were Will Belderson and Ken Bailey with Gerry Cameron again giving us a pleasant surprise by finishing first of the 'B' team in 23rd place.
Ken Bailey seemed to be doing a steady training spin, while the extra miles suited Bernard Eglinton who shows steady improvement on each outing since his return from abroad.
In the Kent Championship, Ken Bailey walked a very fine race to finish 7th over a course which,the winning time of 74:26 by Bob Clark would indicate,is not quite a full 10.

Ken Bailey also after being in fourth position gradually dropped back after a few miles. Ray Middleton came through after a steady start to finish second despite knee trouble, and going off-course in the last half-mile.

Don Bartliff had taken over fourth team position for us, and confirmed that he has all the promise of championships to come in the years ahead; well backed by Ken Bailey, George Beecham, and Will Belderson.
Our R.A.F. member, however, had the edge and at the finish was some 57 seconds clear. Pat Duncan walked extremely well in his first Club 20,finished 8th and carried off the handicap from K.

Ken Bailey also walked a well judged race and was our second man home in 6th position, Bob Farley after a very fast start, faded rather badly in the later stages of the race but held on to finish 8th in third team position.
Vaughan was still ahead at the turn well backed up by Ken Bailey, Bob Farley and Ray Hall, who after a slow start, was beginning to move through the field.
After leading for the first 9 miles Colin Young (Essex B.) was caught by a group of four walkers which included Ray Hall and Ken Bailey (Bels).

Ray Middleton finished 3rd in 3hrs 39mins 49secs without fully extending himself, and with Ken Bailey 5th and Ray Hall 7th also saving himself for the London to Brighton a fortnight ahead, the Bels easily took the team race 9 points to a weakened S.W.C 19 points.

As the clock struck seven a group of six walkers including Ray and Ken Bailey (Bels) followed Colin Young (EB) who was second in 1961 and 1962 across Westminster Bridge, for what was to be the most keenly fought Brighton for many years.
